summary: Round 2. The r1 MAJOR (tests/ci/sweep-shards.test.ts:invalid-weight-cases-cannot-fail) is fixed. The new {x: bad, y: 1} fixture fails when -1 or NaN is kept as is. I checked this by simulation: the mutants 'no >= 0 check', 'no type/finite checks' and 'use the raw value' are all caught. Two mutants survive, 'drop Number.isFinite' and 'drop typeof', but both are equivalent for the values the spec lists (-1, NaN, string), because NaN >= 0 is false and Number.isFinite rejects strings. Only Infinity would tell them apart, and the spec does not ask for that. The new default-weights test can fail: it checks that new WeightedSequencer(ctx) matches assignShards over the committed sweep-weights.json, and that this result differs from the empty-weights split. That catches a constructor that defaults to {} or to the wrong weights. The r1 MINOR tools/ci/sweep-shards.ts:default-weights-untested-injection-param is closed, because the default path is now tested and the injected parameter is used by the worked-example sequencer test. The change since r1 touches only tests/ci/sweep-shards.test.ts, so there is no scope creep. The tests/support/sandbox.ts deviation is unchanged and still acceptable. sweep-shards.test.ts and ci-shards.acceptance.test.ts pass locally (9 tests, one vitest run). gates/fix-8.json is PASS. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
